speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, lower leg swelling, and weight loss. To understand the cause of these symptoms, how long have you been feeling this way?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history. Given your age, chronic bronchitis, and significant weight loss, is there any unintentional night sweats, fever, or change in bowel habits you have noticed?

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work shows significant anemia, low platelets, and severe kidney strain with massive protein loss, while the imaging confirms a 2.5 cm mass in your right upper lobe. Given the weight loss and leg swelling, are you experiencing any recent coughing up of blood, or has your appetite decreased significantly in the last few months?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Lower leg swelling, Unintentional weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The imaging reveals a mass in your right lung, and your urine shows massive protein loss with fatty casts, while your albumin is critically low. Is there a history of smoking, or have you noticed any hemoptysis (coughing up blood)?

text:
You have presented with a lung mass, severe nephrotic syndrome (massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema), and constitutional symptoms like weight loss and fatigue, with negative autoimmune workup. Given your age, the location of the lung mass, and the aggressive nature of the systemic symptoms, have you or your family history any known genetic conditions related to monoclonal gammopathies?
